case_title: Arun Raj v. Union of India and Ors.
accused_occupation: Army personnel: Ex-Signalman (Lance Nayak) in 787 (Independent) Air Defence Brigade Signal Company
accused_victim_relationship: Co-worker (fellow army personnel); prior dispute, as the accused alleged the deceased and another soldier had abused him the previous day
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302; Army Act s.69 (read with s.302 IPC)
evidence_type: Eyewitness; dying declaration; medical evidence; knife recovered as evidence (ME-1)
aggravating_circumstances: Single stab to chest of a sleeping victim with a sharp kitchen knife; knife concealed and brought in deliberately; time to deliberate (40-45 minutes); assault a day after the abuse
trial_court_outcome: General Court Martial found guilty under s.69 Army Act r/w s.302 IPC; initially 7 years RI and dismissal from service; on revision, sentenced to life imprisonment and dismissal from service
high_court_outcome: Writ petition dismissed; conviction under s.302 upheld
offence_finally_established: Murder under s.302 IPC (with s.69 Army Act)
neutral_facts: On 22 March 1998, the accused reported to a section in-charge that the victim and another soldier had abused him with a derogatory word. The section in-charge questioned them and they denied it. The accused also reported a heated exchange with the victim the previous night. Later that day the victim returned to the barrack after lunch and lay on his cot near the door. Another soldier, who had also just returned to the barrack, saw the accused approach the door wearing a half T-shirt and a lungi. The accused took a knife hidden in the lungi and stabbed the sleeping victim once on the right side of the chest. The eyewitness shouted at the accused and others gathered; the accused was separated from the victim, who was taken to hospital and later died. The regimental medical officer testified that the only external injury was the knife wound. The knife, made of iron with a sharp edge, was among the evidence collected. The victim had also given a dying declaration to another soldier, who testified. The eyewitness could not link the stabbing to the earlier abuse or argument. Timing evidence showed about 40 to 45 minutes between the accused's return from the higher officer's office and the stabbing, during which the accused and the victim were in the same barrack without any conversation.
offence_severity: Death or life imprisonment (as stated by the Confirming Authority); no minimum stated
physical_harm: Single stab wound to the right side of the chest; death of the victim
premeditation_planning: Yes. Court found due deliberation and planning: a 40-45 minute gap, concealment of the knife, and an attack a day after the abuse
motive: Revenge for the humiliation of the alleged abuse ('Gandu') the previous day, as accepted by the Court
key_evidence_accepted: Eyewitness account of PW-1 (as to the stabbing and timing); medical evidence of PW-9 (single stab wound); knife evidence (ME-1); dying declaration to PW-3
witness_credibility: High Court found PW-1 and PW-3 reliable. Supreme Court relied on PW-1's account and the cross-examination of PW-9 without separately assessing credibility
trial_duration: offence: 22.3.1998; trial judgment: not given (General Court Martial revised sentence order dated 15.1.1999); High Court: 25.8.2005; Supreme Court: 13.05.2010
legal_representation: Accused: K.K. Mani, Ankit Swarup, K. Lakshminarayan. Union of India: Brijender Chahar, R. Balasubramaniyam, Naresh Kaushik, Anil Katiyar, D.S. Mahra
investigation_status: FIR registered; investigation completed; charge-sheet prepared and forwarded to the Judicial Magistrate; court martial proceedings initiated
appeal_history: Trial (General Court Martial): convicted, 7 years RI and dismissal, revised to life and dismissal on revision; Confirming Authority confirmed; petition to Chief of Army Staff rejected. High Court: writ petition dismissed. Supreme Court: appeal dismissed
prosecution_argument: Findings and punishment should stand; the evidence proves an offence under s.302 IPC; judicial review is limited and cannot re-appreciate the Court Martial evidence
defence_argument: Grave and sudden provocation brings the case under Exception I to s.300 IPC; alternatively s.304 Part II applies as there was no intention to cause death, given a single blow
legal_principle_applied: Exception I to s.300 (grave and sudden provocation, judged by a reasonable person's reaction and time to cool); s.304 Part II ingredients; Virsa Singh 'thirdly' test (intention to cause a bodily injury sufficient to cause death); a single blow is not decisive
precedent_relied_upon: Relied on: State of Rajasthan v. Dhool Singh (2004) 12 SCC 546; Virsa Singh v. State of Punjab AIR 1958 SC 465; Anil v. State of Haryana (2007) 10 SCC 274. Also cited: Mancini v DPP (1942) AC 200; Rex v Lesbini (1914) 3 KB 1116. Distinguished: Bhera; Kunhayippu; Masumsha Hasansha; Guljar Hussain; K. Ramakrishnan Unnithan; Pappu; Muthu
sentencing_rationale: Not stated (the Court addressed only conviction and dismissed the appeal; no sentencing reasoning given)
judicial_aggravating_factors: Due deliberation and planning; assault a day after the alleged abuse; vital body part (chest); deadly weapon; victim asleep
